name: Walking pad

lead: A walking pad is a slim, low-speed folding treadmill without handrails, designed to slide under a desk or sofa. Speeds usually top out at about 6 km/h.
It is used to add steady walking to desk days, increasing daily steps without leaving the home. For appearance, the stated appeal is more daily energy expenditure and less sitting.

paras: Walking at a slow pace increases energy expenditure above sitting, roughly 100 kcal per hour more in a pooled analysis of treadmill-desk lab studies, and reduces sitting time. Reviews of treadmill desks show small improvements in sitting time and some metabolic markers. No trials of walking pads specifically were found, so the closest research on treadmill desks is used.

Typing accuracy and mouse precision can decline while walking, and productivity effects are mixed. Lower-priced units may overheat, have overstated weight limits and be loud. The claim of thousands of extra fat-burning steps is plausible, but fat loss depends on diet and total activity; slow walking is a modest calorie burn.
